_doc: Lords' seats on the town map (world/innerMap/seats.js): manors and the castle of a capital. seatTypes: the buildings that are seats. doorGuards[type]: how many stand at its door day and night (titles: what they're called). A manor's doors are barred when nobody is at home (no one inside: the lord and household go about the town by day); a castle always keeps its garrison. While its guards stand, they turn the player away by night (nightFrom/nightTo hours) or with a warrant out in the realm, and let them in otherwise; knock the guards down and the door is yours (still barred if nobody is home). Whoever holds the seat (it is theirs, or their colony, or their crown's town) always walks in. lines: what the guards say ({lord} = the lord's name or 'the lord', {seat} = the building's name). zones: places in the castle the player may not go (tile._zone; ui/innerMapZones.js) — castle_private, the lord's chambers and the treasury: a castle guard warns, then attacks. staff: who keeps the castle inside (role → [count, npc type]); names for them.

castles._doc: Castles come late (world/castles.js): before a capital's year it keeps its seat in its lord's great hall (a manor on the town map, an unwalled town on the world map). Each capital is due its castle in startYear + a hash of the town x spread; it rises in the first year after that when its crown can pay cost from the treasury (into the capital's purse: the builders are paid in town). A world made after the year starts with it standing. It takes buildYears to raise: each year the crown pays cost / buildYears to the builders (a year it cannot, the work stands still; settlement.castleWorks).

away: {lord} is not at home. No one goes in while the house is empty.
The house is shut up. Come back when {lord} is in.
Nobody's home, and nobody's going in. Move along.
barred: The doors of {seat} are barred, and no one answers your knock.
night: At this hour? {lord} receives no one. Come back in the morning.
The house is abed. Off with you till daylight.
Gates are shut for the night. Try again at dawn.
warrant: I know your face. There's a warrant out on you — clear off before I call the watch.
Not you. Not with the crown wanting words with you.
admit: State your business. ...Very well, go in. Mind your manners.
{lord} is in. Go on, and wipe your boots.
In you go. Keep your hands where we can see them.
unguarded: No one stands at the door. You slip inside.
welcome: Your house, my lord. All is well.

warn: Those are the lord's own rooms. Out!
Halt! No one goes there without leave.
Back to the hall, you. Now.
castle_private.warnNote: Go back to the great hall.
castle_private.attackNote: You were told to keep to the hall.
